descriptionHtml:
Approach · OAT-01 Signing In & Session Security · S22 A real phone with a wrong clock or time zone does not change when a session ends

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U3 After 12 hours idle, the physician has to sign in again with an email OTP. (UAT OAT-01 step 3; UAT OAT-01 Expected; TFA-94513 AC 4) — gate: blocked: TFA-94513 in progress
  • U4 At 30 days the session hard-expires, however active it is. On day 31, access needs a new email OTP. (UAT OAT-01 step 4; UAT OAT-01 Expected; TFA-94513 AC 5) — gate: blocked: TFA-94513 in progress

Test design technique: Error guessing (error-guessing) — Go straight for the places most likely to break (failures, double clicks, two tabs, a wrong clock, injected instructions).

Given A phone (store or TestFlight build) and a browser signed in to the same account. The phone's clock is set +13 h, then +31 d, then -2 d, then to another time zone.

When Use the app after each clock change; then age the session on the server and use it again with the clock set back

Then A fresh session stays usable whatever the device clock says. An aged session is refused whatever the device clock says. Both devices show the same state.

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): UAT 3.8 (server clock for every time-based rule) applied to U3 / U4. Any sign-out caused only by the device clock, or an aged session kept alive by setting the clock back, = Fail. The browser half runs as S07 cell (e).

Where it ran: dev; test method DEVICE · Real device (iOS / Android); lane planned in the matrix: manual (manual)

S22 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/OAT-01.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Environment: dev — dev deployment, build e02167f (Deploy Convex, 2026-10-12T18:24:27Z); account and address are not written into the report; run folder runs/2026-10-14-dev.

Test method: DEVICE · Real device (iOS / Android); secondary: TIME · Time / aging (clock moved) — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on dev; Source: dev.
